visual_action: Former President Barack Obama stands at a podium speaking to a crowd. The podium has a sign that reads "Georgia VOTES EARLY". He smiles and gestures as he responds to a comment from an unseen audience member.

cast.name: Barack Obama
cast.evidence: Barack Obama is the sole person clearly shown on screen, speaking for the duration of the video.

cast.name: unnamed audience member
cast.evidence: An unidentified voice from the crowd yells, "We love you!" at the start of the clip.

on_screen_text.text: but I still want you to vote!

spoken_summary: An audience member shouts, "We love you!" to Barack Obama. He replies, "I love you too, but I still want you to vote!" The crowd cheers in response.
audio_music: The audio consists entirely of dialogue and the sounds of a cheering crowd at a political rally. There is no music.
editing_pacing: The video is a single, static shot with no cuts or edits.
central_claim: While the affection between a political leader and his supporters is valued, the most important action supporters can take is to vote.
intended_effect: To leverage Barack Obama's popularity to create a feeling of connection and motivate people, specifically in Georgia, to vote.
